questions.stem: A car travels around a circular roundabout at a steady 30 km/h. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Both speed and velocity are constant
Speed is constant but velocity is changing
Speed is changing but velocity is constant
Both speed and velocity are changing

questions.explanation: Speed is a scalar — it only has magnitude, which stays at 30 km/h. Velocity is a vector — it has both magnitude and direction. As the car goes around the roundabout, its direction constantly changes, so velocity is constantly changing even though speed is constant. This is a key distinction between scalars and vectors.

questions.stem: Two forces act on a box: 12 N to the right and 5 N upward. What is the magnitude of the resultant force?
questions.explanation: These forces are perpendicular, so we use Pythagoras' theorem: R = sqrt(12² + 5²) = sqrt(144 + 25) = sqrt(169) = 13 N. Option (c) of 17 N is the common mistake of simply adding the magnitudes, which only works when forces are in the same direction. Option (a) of 7 N is the result of subtracting, which only applies to opposite directions.

questions.stem: Which of the following lists contains ONLY vector quantities?
questions.explanation: Displacement, velocity, and momentum all have both magnitude and direction, making them vectors. Option (a) is wrong because speed is a scalar. Option (c) is wrong because mass and distance are scalars (weight is a vector, though). Option (d) is wrong because energy is a scalar.

questions.stem: A swimmer crosses a river heading due north at 3 m/s. The river current flows due east at 4 m/s. What is the swimmer's resultant speed?
questions.explanation: The velocities are perpendicular (north and east), so we use Pythagoras' theorem: R = sqrt(3² + 4²) = sqrt(9 + 16) = sqrt(25) = 5 m/s. This is a classic 3-4-5 right triangle. Simply adding (7 m/s) would be incorrect because the vectors are at right angles, not in the same direction.

questions.stem: A force of 20 N acts at 30° above the horizontal. What is the horizontal component of this force?
questions.explanation: The horizontal component is found using: F_x = F cos(theta) = 20 × cos(30°) = 20 × 0.866 = 17.3 N. Option (a) of 10.0 N is the vertical component (20 × sin 30° = 10 N). A common error is mixing up sine and cosine when resolving vectors — cosine gives the component adjacent to the angle.
